boundaries.purpose: Explicit CUDA resource adapter for allocation, pinned staging, streams, events, graphs, deterministic cuBLASLt, and generation-checked borrowed launch tokens. Seen owns policy, ownership, cache identity, fallback, and diagnostics. Token borrowing only validates lifetime and device identity; it does not allocate or synchronize CUDA work. CPU-only builds neither discover nor link the adapter. RTX 4090 foundation and separate model-adapter canaries exercise it. Experimental until hardware certification.

Direct Vulkan 1.2 loader ABI; Seen owns bounded metadata, explicit software admission, provider identities, device/context lifetimes, quotas and cleanup. Borrowed create-info/output pointers expire on return; instance/device handles are consumed exactly once. SDK layout oracle, malformed-metadata fuzz and Mesa software reference cover Linux x86-64. No GPU execution certification. Permanent vendor ABI; no C policy adapter.

Per-call Linux PR_SVE_GET_VL normalization copies the calling thread vector length into a borrowed UInt64 output and clears it on failure. No allocations or retained pointers. Seen validates lengths, discovers capabilities, chooses fallback, computes kernels and owns progress. Other platforms return unsupported. Covered by changing-length/errno/null-output mocks, metadata fuzz and SIMD fixtures. Permanent OS ABI until direct compiler normalization preserves these rules.

Generation-checked pthread lifetime, Linux affinity/NUMA calls and opaque TLS identity. Seen owns task slots, fixed workers, typed admission, scheduling, cancellation and cleanup. Failed joins retain ownership. Linux x86-64 and macOS x86-64/arm64; macOS accepts inherited placement only. Executor/native lifetime and I/O worker suites cover this permanent OS boundary. macOS execution remains uncertified.

Linux kernel AIO request struct normalization, io_setup/submit/cancel/getevents/destroy and semaphore eventfd calls. Seen owns fixed request slots, buffer/descriptor/request storage, alignment and transfer budgets, generation tokens, cancellation state, completion progress, leases and cleanup. Only explicit O_DIRECT descriptors are accepted; unsupported kernels/targets fail explicitly.

POSIX spawn action/attribute normalization, explicit pipe endpoints, Linux pidfd open/signal and waitpid result decoding. Seen owns packed argv/envp storage, absolute-program validation, bounded live-child quotas, blocking-pool admission, every construction prefix, pipe ownership, cancellation and reaping. No shell, PATH search, implicit environment, task scheduler or detached child. Software probes cover explicit child I/O and pidfd cancellation.

Direct Linux epoll/eventfd OS normalization with no native registration table, slot lookup, timer storage, work queue or scheduling. Seen owns event-buffer memory, indexed generation identities, registration ownership, bounded producer leases, deadline heap and ready FIFO. OS wake saturation coalesces without allocation. Native probes cover one-shot deregistration, raw identity retention, wake coalescing and handle counts.

Nonblocking TCP socket OS calls and packed IPv4/IPv6 sockaddr normalization. Seen owns address validation, bounded transfers, partial progress, event-loop admission, timer heap, descriptor ownership, cancellation and worker dispatch. Linux x86-64 only; other targets return unsupported. No DNS, protocol, retry loop or scheduler in this adapter. Connected UDP datagrams and OS entropy are normalized here; DNS wire policy stays in Seen.

Single nonblocking pipe/socket read/write calls and per-thread SIGPIPE normalization. Seen owns checked owning spans, buffer offsets and limits, context checks, 64-bit progress, retry policy, descriptor lifetime and readiness integration. Regular files/devices and blocking descriptors are rejected. Native probes verify partial reads/writes, saturation, closed-peer behavior and preservation of a previously pending SIGPIPE.

Existing runtime pool deallocation releases exactly the 16-byte compiler-created trait box owned by a DotClockHandle or DotBackendHandle. The concrete provider remains caller-owned and must outlive the handle. Seen owns dispatch, provider lifetime rules, progress and error policy. Contract allocation baselines and sanitizer profiles cover native and deterministic providers. Permanent until compiler-managed borrowed trait boxes replace explicit handle cleanup; migrate creation and release together.

Explicit C-string ownership: conversion to C allocates a copy, conversion to Seen borrows. Seen releaseArgs consumes copied argument snapshots, pairing each malloc free with allocation-budget release before freeing array storage. Seen owns the loop and lifetimes; native symbols only free storage and adjust accounting. Packaged CUDA-string tests, repeated argument snapshots and ASan verify cleanup. Permanent until compiler-managed owners replace both allocation and release.

Existing array-data accessor borrows exclusive Array<Int> storage without allocation or retention. Seen validates byte domains and the 32 MiB ceiling, compacts forward, clones a length-delimited string view, and frees the input once. No resize or alias is permitted. All-octet, NUL, empty, rejection and allocation tests cover it. Permanent runtime layout projection until a portable bootstrap array-data intrinsic replaces this accessor and its owner together.

Seen job owners capture the compiler's immutable two-pointer dyn box. bind checks its first data word against the concrete Send job before transport; only that owner restores dispatch and frees the 16-byte box. take transfers the concrete job; release calls its destructor first. Existing pool ABI only; no native policy. Alias, rejection, cancellation and live-allocation regressions cover ownership. Retain until the compiler provides an owned existential ABI.

Bounded process-start snapshots, Linux process replacement after validated deterministic CLI activation, and symlink-aware path containment. Native Seen owns grants, policy, context identity, diagnostics, and observable values. The runtime captures inputs before user code, re-execs without PATH lookup when the flag activates the mode, and canonicalizes existing paths through the OS. Unsupported process replacement and Windows path policy fail closed.

Narrow OS adapter for move-only file handles, metadata, positional and direct I/O, allocation, durability, locks, directory iteration, links, and filesystem identification. Native Seen owns raw-path validation, bounds, traversal, temporary naming, atomic replacement, recursive operations, gather sequencing, fallback policy, diagnostics, and cleanup. Exercised by sparse files above 4 GiB, aligned O_DIRECT, hostile paths, crash-safe replacement, and ext4/XFS certification.

Thread-local allocation events with recursion protection and exclusive registration. Seen owns bounded address lookup, allocator provenance, heap/count limits, parser scratch restoration and release. No native ownership list or parsing policy. GPU lowering returns independent IR before temporary cleanup. Repeated success/rejection and four growing map shapes check exact accounting under sanitizers. Also owns immutable CLI snapshots. Permanent callback ABI; serial parser sessions only.

Minimal allocation ABI for move-only aligned Seen buffers. Seen validates geometry and alignment and owns lifetime policy; the runtime only performs platform-correct allocation and free. Exercised by layout, alignment, move, and leak tests. Permanent until compiler-owned allocation intrinsics can preserve the same C ABI.

Direct Darwin open, fstat, F_NOCACHE and positional pread/pwrite only. Seen owns regular-file and cache policy, checked geometry, admission, worker budgets, synchronous borrow lifetime, cancellation, partial results and deterministic drain. The shared Seen worker queue reuses the executor. Other platforms fail explicitly with Darwin error vocabulary. No retries, scheduler, allocation policy, io_uring emulation or hidden fallback. Contract/fuzz/native fixtures cover this permanent OS boundary.

Direct Linux io_uring syscalls, mappings, eventfd, page size, descriptor duplication and shared-memory atomics. Seen owns UAPI encoding, checked geometry, page-rounded mapping and worker budgets, submission, cancellation, completion, leases and partial cleanup. Other platforms fail explicitly. No liburing, retry, scheduler or fallback policy. Contract/fuzz/native fixtures cover this permanent OS boundary; hardware certification remains separate.

Direct Win32 IOCP creation/association/dequeue, overlapped ReadFile/WriteFile, CancelIoEx, UTF-8 to UTF-16 ABI normalization and CreateFileW. Seen owns bounded OVERLAPPED storage, generation keys, fresh file ownership, admission, error classification, cancellation and drain ordering. Non-Windows targets fail explicitly. No scheduler, allocation policy or fallback. Contract/fuzz/native fixtures cover the permanent OS boundary; Windows execution certification remains separate.

Bounded C-library decimal-to-binary conversion after native Seen JSON syntax validation. No storage escapes; invalid bounds, incomplete conversion, overflow, and underflow return NaN, which the Seen parser maps to a stable range error. Exercised by FEL-507 malformed-number sanitizer and soak cases. Permanent until native Seen supplies a correctly rounded bounded conversion; migrate parser and symbol together.

Runtime allocation ABI for JSON-owned strings. Parser, serializer, and incremental-builder flattening, cloning, and owned character encoding return pool storage that release frees exactly once; borrowed strings never cross as owned. Exercised under ASan/UBSan by the FEL-507 tiny-object and FEL-543 safetensors lifetime regressions. Permanent until native Seen owned/move string semantics replace it; migrate all callers and symbols together.
Emit and optimize LLVM IR for native targets.

Large-file-safe file and mapped-window ownership adapter with stable status codes, checked offsets, truncation validation, advisory paging, page locking, and optional NUMA binding. Seen owns bounds, retry, placement, and cleanup policy. Exercised with sparse files above 60 GiB, truncation, busy-close, lock, advice, and cleanup cases.

Read live checked-out allocation bytes independently from recyclable slab reserve without changing the physical memory limit or swap policy. The runtime reports a nonallocating fixed-layout snapshot and retained slab capacity; native Seen owns resource lifetime, failure policy, and cleanup tests.

Compiler-lowered bounded worker dispatch adapter. Native Seen/compiler semantics prove captures, select the fixed worker bound, preserve the environment lifetime, and fail closed on every nonzero result; the runtime mechanically partitions the supplied finite range, creates and joins OS threads, and reports the lowest body error or a stable resource status without sequential fallback.
Contain compiler child-process creation during guarded rebuilds.

Narrow epoll, kqueue, IOCP, wakeup, native-handle, and native-handle ABI. Native Seen owns bounds, registration generations, readiness/completion scheduling, timers, fairness, cancellation, fallback policy, diagnostics, and exactly-once cleanup. Exercised by named cross-platform capability fixtures plus Linux readiness, stale-generation, cancellation, sanitizer, leak, and 30-sample wakeup contracts.

Release compiler-owned string and repr(C) aggregate boxes inside erased Result containers. The runtime adapter validates the storage layout and performs one size-aware accounted free; native Seen owns the payload semantics, release decision, and container lifetime.

Narrow generation-checked OS synchronization adapter for atomics, mutexes, conditions, reader/writer locks, and native thread identity. Native Seen owns Send and Share legality, ownership, capacity, cancellation, deadlines, channels, poisoning, lock ranks, deadlock diagnostics, scheduling, and cleanup. Exercised by native, UBSan, ASan, stale-handle, timeout, contention, cross-platform compile, and zero-live-resource contracts.

Narrow clock and sleep normalization ABI. Native Seen owns checked duration geometry, injected/manual clocks, timer queue bounds, structured-async deadlines, missed-tick policy, RFC3339 parsing, cancellation, and backoff. The runtime only reads monotonic/wall clocks and performs an interrupt-safe sleep.

Startup CPUID/XGETBV normalization and read-only feature queries require OS-enabled XCR0 state before Seen selects AVX bodies. No allocations or borrowed storage escape; process-lifetime feature data initializes before workers. Seen owns dispatch, fallback, kernels, bounds, progress and diagnostics. Simulated OS-state probes and SIMD fixtures cover the boundary. Migrate queries together if compiler CPU discovery replaces this ABI.
